jobs.title: AI Engineer (LLM Agents & RAG)
jobs.description:
About The Role

You will design and build AI agents that do real work for our clients: answering support questions from their own documents, qualifying leads, screening candidates and handing over to a person at the right moment. This is production engineering, not research. Every agent you build ships to real users and has to keep working.

What you will do

Build agents that answer from client data using retrieval, tools and clear guardrails.
Connect agents to the systems clients already use, such as help desks, CRMs and WhatsApp.
Create test sets from real conversations, and measure quality before and after every change.
Monitor live agents, review conversations and improve answers over time.
Explain trade-offs to clients in plain language.

You might be a good fit if

You have shipped LLM-based features to production and know why some of them failed.
You are comfortable in TypeScript or Python, and with APIs, queues and databases.
You care about evaluation, not just demos.
You can work in weekly increments and enjoy showing your work.

Nice to have

Experience with retrieval, embeddings and vector or hybrid search.
Experience with Zendesk, Intercom or the WhatsApp Business Platform.

How we work

A remote-first team, working with clients in the US, UK and India.
We ship working software every week and show it to the client.
Clients own the source code and infrastructure we build, so we earn our next project by doing this one well.

jobs.title: Agentic AI Engineer, Vice President
jobs.description:
About The Role

We are hiring a Vice President (VP), Agentic AI Engineering, for our GenAI Center of Excellence at State Street. As VP, you will own the strategy and architecture of our enterprise agentic AI platform, setting the vision for multi-agent orchestration, security, and governance. This is a senior leadership role where you will influence technology direction across the organization, lead engineering talent, and foster innovation in agentic AI on AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure.

Key Responsibilities

Own the enterprise agentic platform strategy, including architecture, technology roadmap, and governance standards, with a focus on multi-cloud (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure) scalability and resilience.
Exposure to agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, Langraph, GoogleADK) and drive innovation in multi-agent orchestration at scale.
Set and monitor organizational standards for multi-agent orchestration, A2A protocols, HITL, tenant IAM/RBAC, and runtime security across cloud platforms.
Represent the Agent Foundry and Runtime pods in executive and cross-functional governance forums, influencing cloud adoption and strategy.
Drive platform-wide reliability, scalability, and cost optimization initiatives for agentic AI workloads across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure.
Build, lead, and develop engineering leadership talent across the pods.
Partner with Architecture, Data/Knowledge, and Product teams for end-to-end platform strategy and delivery, ensuring alignment of cloud and agentic stack adoption.
Foster innovation and continuous improvement, promoting technical excellence and emerging best practices for cloud-native agentic platforms.
Oversee compliance, risk, and performance reviews for agentic AI at the organizational level, including across public cloud environments.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field; advanced degrees a plus.
12–17 years of relevant experience, including leadership of large-scale, multi-agent or AI-driven platforms.
Proficient in Python and familiar with at least one additional modern programming language (such as Java, Go, or C++).
Proven strategic ownership of platform architecture and technology roadmaps, with deep knowledge of agentic AI systems.
Extensive hands-on and leadership experience with multi-cloud environments (AWS, Google Cloud, Azure), including security, governance, and cost optimization.
Demonstrated success in setting organizational standards for reliability, scalability, and incident management in AI systems.
Experience partnering with executive and cross-functional teams on platform strategy and delivery.
Track record of building and developing engineering leadership talent and fostering innovation.
Expertise in compliance, risk management, and performance oversight for enterprise AI solutions.
Exceptional communication, governance, and stakeholder management skills.

About State Street

Across the globe, institutional investors rely on us to help them manage risk, respond to challenges, and drive performance and profitability. We keep our clients at the heart of everything we do, and smart, engaged employees are essential to our continued success.

We are committed to fostering an environment where every employee feels valued and empowered to reach their full potential. As an essential partner in our shared success, you’ll benefit from inclusive development opportunities, flexible work-life support, paid volunteer days, and vibrant employee networks that keep you connected to what matters most. Join us in shaping the future.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we consider all qualified applicants for all positions without regard to race, creed, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, age, disability, genetic information, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, citizenship, marital status, domestic partnership or civil union status, familial status, military and veteran status, and other characteristics protected by applicable law.

jobs.title: Software Engineer with a Public Open-Source Track Record (Remote, Part-Time)
jobs.description:
If you have real, attributable code in public repositories, this is a well-paid way to use that experience part-time from anywhere.

The short version

A remote contract, around 15 hours a week, weekends fine, paid hourly at a three-figure rate (from $100/hour). The job is to create, solve and grade demanding software-engineering tasks that are used to train and test AI systems that write code.

The work

Expect to spend your time inside repositories you have never seen before: figuring out how they are put together, following data through services, libraries and databases, reproducing bugs, fixing them in a way the maintainers would merge, and writing the tests to prove it. Some tasks ask you to port a complete implementation from one language to another. Others ask you to judge whether a machine-generated patch is correct, complete, secure and something you would accept in review.

Who we are looking for

The single hard requirement is a public code portfolio (GitHub or similar) showing substantial code you wrote or maintain in open-source projects. Docs-only, formatting and dependency-bump contributions do not count. Beyond that:

• Strong engineering in at least one substantial area (frontend, backend, systems, infra, developer tooling, etc.)

• Fluency in several languages; common ones on this project are TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C#, C++ and Ruby

• You write proper automated tests, from unit to end-to-end

• You are comfortable reviewing code written by people and by machines

Terms

Independent contractor, hourly ($100+/hr), fewer than 20 hours a week, remote. Work is in English.

To apply, submit through OpenTrain with a link to your public repositories.
